subject: Tenant initialization, network criteria, and ops primer
messages:
From: Carl Jenkins <carl.jenkins@blueoak.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara.patel@blueoak.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Tenant initialization and edge network criteria

Hi Vivek / Ben,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. We're kicking off the tenant initialization work for our private edge deployment and want to make sure we capture network and ops constraints up front so your preflight isn't blocked. High-level asks from our side:

- Confirm required outbound egress IPs and ports for token retrieval and runtime telemetry.
- Guidance on CIDR sizing (recommended minimums for subnets and host pools).
- Any mandatory NAT / proxy or BGP requirements for dedicated edge nodes.
- KMS integration model and whether we can bring our own HSM.
- Preferred maintenance windows for smoke tests and initial traffic cutover.

I've attached a basic network diagram and we can fill details after you share the template/checklist. Attached: blueoak-network-diagram.pdf

Can you share a concise ops primer and the tenant-init template so my infra team can populate values? Looking to schedule the preflight run during the week of Nov 30 if that works.

Cheers,
Carl Jenkins
Cloud Architect | BlueOak Health
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Carl Jenkins <carl.jenkins@blueoak.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Tenant initialization and edge network criteria

Carl — thanks, this is perfect. I've attached our tenant-init-template.xlsx and a short ops primer (see preflight-smoke-script.txt referenced below). Summary of the key prerequisites and items we need from BlueOak before we run a preflight: 

1) Network & IPs
- CIDR allocation: recommended /22 for control plane + /24 per node pool for initial staging (can be adjusted for larger fleets).
- Egress: we require a static set of outbound IPs for token exchange, metrics, and deployment webhooks. Ports: 443 outbound (TLS) plus 123 for NTP if your environment blocks NTP over NAT.
- Allowlist endpoints: auth.redwood-inference.com, metrics.redwood-inference.com, s3-compatible endpoints (we'll provide exact FQDNs once account is created).

2) Connectivity patterns
- Preferred: Direct VPC peering between BlueOak VPC and Redwood-managed peering VPC.
- Alternate: NAT + proxy with TLS passthrough for egress (if peering not permitted).
- BGP: Optional. Only required for advanced routing or multi-homed WANs; call it out if you run BGP at the edge.

3) Security & Keying
- KMS: BYOK supported via Cloud HSM or KMS connector. We need a service principal with decrypt permissions scoped to the tenant key.
- Certificates: TLS cert for control-plane domain or ability to provision via ACM/managed TLS.
- Audit: log forwarder endpoint (syslog/HTTPS) if you require hosted logging only.

4) Operational access
- Jump host: we ask for a bastion/jumpbox to be reachable from our ops range during the preflight window (temporary rule with start/end times preferred).
- Service accounts: IAM role or service account that can manage routes and create DNS records in your hosted zone for health checks.

5) Time & scheduling
- Maintenance windows: nominate a 3-hour window for the preflight smoke run; we aim for 75–90 minutes of active tests plus rollback buffer.

Next steps:
- Fill the tenant-init-template.xlsx with IP ranges, NTP/proxy details, and contact windows.
- We will send a detailed endpoints list (FQDNs + IPs) once a tenant record is provisioned.

I'll coordinate internally with Ben (network lead) and Marissa (ops lead) on the smoke script and acceptance criteria. Proposed preflight: 2026-11-30 02:00–05:00 UTC (Nov 30 local). If that conflicts, propose alternatives.

Attachments: tenant-init-template.xlsx, preflight-smoke-script.txt

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Sr. Product Manager, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Carl Jenkins <carl.jenkins@blueoak.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T11:38:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Tenant initialization and edge network criteria

Carl — quick clarifications from the network side (keeping short):

- NAT/BGP: If you plan to use NAT only, confirm whether source NAT is per-node or per-VPC. Per-node SNAT complicates port reuse for some gRPC flows.
- Peering: If using VPC peering, we need a route table snapshot for the VPCs involved and an ASG for node-to-control communication.
- DNS: Are you okay with split-horizon DNS? We prefer to create an internal subdomain (e.g., redwood-internal.blueoak) for health-check endpoints — we'll need DNS delegation privileges or an API key to create records.

Marissa / Karthik — tagging you for smoke-test ownership and any firewall rule templates we usually provide to customers.

-ben

Subject: Re: Tenant initialization and edge network criteria

Thanks everyone — answering Ben's bullets and filling the template basics. Per the attached tenant-init-template.xlsx (sheet: network):

- CIDR blocks: control plane 10.40.0.0/22; node pool A 10.41.0.0/24; node pool B 10.42.0.0/24.
- Egress: BlueOak will provide a SNAT pool of 3 static IPs for outbound (stable NAT per-VPC). We'll open 443 outbound; UDP 123 to NTP servers.
- BGP: Not used in initial phase — single-homed WAN through our edge NVA.
- DNS: We can create delegated subdomain; will provide DNS API key with limited perms (route create/update).
- KMS: We have an HSM appliance; security has approved a connector model — Sara and I will coordinate the KMS onboarding docs.

Attachments: completed network sheet (see tenant-init-template.xlsx) and blueoak-network-diagram.pdf.

Request: can Redwood send a short firewall allowlist (CIDR + ports) that we can drop into the rule ticket? Also confirm whether the preflight requires inbound ports to be opened to Redwood's ops jump range — if so we'll create a time-limited rule.

Proposed preflight window still Nov 30; we can shift to Dec 1 if you need extra time.

Thanks,
Carl Jenkins
Cloud Architect | BlueOak Health

Perfect — thanks for filling the sheet, Carl. A few action items and confirmations before we lock the preflight: 

- Firewall allowlist: we'll send an allowlist fixture today (exact FQDNs and IPs). For initial tests you need these outbound ports: 443 (TLS), 443 (webhooks), and 123 (NTP). No inbound ports required except the temporary bastion access window — we'll request a 2-hour window starting at the smoke run time.
- Jump host: yes, we'll need a temporary bastion rule limited to these IPs: 34.82.10.9/32, 34.82.10.10/32 (ops jump range).
- KMS: Sara — let's sync tomorrow; we'll need the connector details and a test key with decrypt-only perms for the tenant; no key rotation during the preflight.

Schedule: we will run the preflight on 2026-11-30 at 02:00 UTC as proposed. Marissa will lead the smoke script and will post results into JIRA-ENG-1284. If anything changes we will update the Drive folder and ping your ticketing queue.

Next steps (owner):
- Redwood: finalize allowlist + preflight runbook (Vivek / Ben)
- BlueOak: confirm bastion window and finalize HSM connector info (Carl / Sara)
- Both: populate tenant-init-template.xlsx (done), confirm DNS delegation tickets

I'll follow up with the allowlist fixture and the preflight runbook link in the next hour.

Thanks all,
Vivek Kulkarni
Sr. Product Manager, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
